\[
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases}
  s_1 \, I / r_1 & I \le r_1 \\
  s_1 + (s_2 - s_1)\,\dfrac{I - r_1}{r_2 - r_1} & r_1 < I \le r_2 \\
  s_2 + (255 - s_2)\,\dfrac{I - r_2}{255 - r_2} & I > r_2
\end{cases}
\qquad
(r_1, s_1) = (64, 32),\ (r_2, s_2) = (192, 224)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input value from 0 to 255
- \((r_1, s_1), (r_2, s_2)\): The two control points, input and output

The curve runs in straight lines through (0, 0), (r1, s1), (r2, s2) and (255, 255), the contrast stretching of Gonzalez and Woods. A middle segment steeper than 45 degrees raises the contrast of the values it covers. When r1 is above r2, the two points swap. With r1 = r2, s1 = 0 and s2 = 255, the curve jumps from 0 to 255 and becomes a threshold. When r1 is 0, the value 0 maps to s1. When r2 is 255, the value 255 maps to s2.
